# Plan: plan-carry-forward

Goal: Decide whether sofar_update_plan should carry existing phase and task status forward. plan_updated is a full replace: mcp/update-plan.ts appends the caller's payload verbatim with no carry-forward, and core/fold.ts:1085-1091 rebuilds phases and tasks defaulting a missing status to pending — so a replan that OMITS statuses silently erases progress, and nothing warns. MEASURED 2026-08-13 over 41 records and 85 plan_updated events, on the payload rather than on folded state: ZERO occurrences, in both the omitted shape and the rename shape. Only 4 plan_updated events ever omit a status at all, and none of the 54 displacements sits in one. So this is PREVENTION with no incident to repair and nothing racing. The live question is therefore whether to build at all, and what to build that does not have to guess identity across a rename — which the payload cannot support, a rename and a delete-plus-add being byte-identical. The full-replace contract is what SPEC's forward-compatibility story rests on (task-drop-state D2), so changing it is a Decision, not a patch. Promoted as phase-lifecycle M2.

Progress: 1/9 tasks done (11%)

## Phase 2 — The ruling [pending] — 0/3 done

- [ ] 2.1 DECIDE the mechanism, against a measured incident count of ZERO — so (d) is a serious answer and not a cop-out, and the burden is on any option that adds code. (a) Merge at the TOOL boundary: fold current state and carry status forward for matching phase names and task ids unless the caller supplies one; the appended payload stays a COMPLETE plan, so the on-disk full-replace contract and replay determinism are untouched. (b) Merge in the FOLD: the one option that changes how every historical log folds, and therefore the one that can break replay determinism. (c) Detect only: warn at the boundary when a resolved entry would leave the plan. (d) Nothing: document the convention. Log the decision citing task-drop-state D2 and phase-lifecycle M2.
- [ ] 2.2 DECIDE what protects the closes already written, if 2.1 leaves any window open. 34 phase closes across 16 STILL-ACTIVE records are the concrete thing this initiative exists to stop losing. 1.1 shows nothing has ever been lost this way, so the honest question is whether this needs anything beyond 2.1 at all — answer it explicitly rather than by assumption.
- [ ] 2.3 DECIDE what happens across a RENAME, at its real size: the mechanism is real and its occurrence count is ZERO, same as omission. The residual is narrow and specific — a fully-explicit payload proves the author was writing statuses deliberately for the entries they INCLUDED, not that they noticed one leaving; a careless rename inside a fully-stated plan writes the new name with whatever was typed and nothing says a resolved name just left. Weigh that against a mechanism that would have to guess identity across a rename, which the payload cannot support. Deciding to do NOTHING is legitimate; it must be a decision rather than an oversight.
